clue.text: President finding extremists in England exhausted

parts.note: either of the two US presidents named Bush

indicators.note: extremists are the people at the far ends, so only the outermost letters of the following word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: A tired head of state touring England is worn out by the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushed is informal slang for being completely tired out, so it is a synonym of exhausted.

clue.text: Plot to nab Republican near Alaska's capital city

indicators.note: to nab is to grab hold of, so the first word ends up holding the next one inside it

parts.note: a plot of ground in a garden, as in a flower bed
standard abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: a capital letter is the one at the head of a word, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the state's name

explanation.surface: A political conspiracy to seize a Republican near the seat of government in Alaska.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital city' reads as one phrase about Juneau, but 'capital' belongs to the wordplay and 'city' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Breda is a historic city in the southern Netherlands, so it is an example of the defining word.

clue.text: Affair with a female outlaw finally ending

parts.note: the pronoun for a female
to outlaw something is to ban it

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the next word, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A romance with a female bandit that eventually comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun for a female bandit, but it works as a verb meaning prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang is informal for a whole business or matter, as in 'the whole shebang', so it can stand for an affair.

clue.text: Murder of Austrian leader included in revised timeline

indicators.note: something included in another is placed within it, so this letter goes inside the other letters
a revised version has been reworked, so the letters of the following word get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter of the nationality word is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A history book's new chronology now includes the assassination of an Austrian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an Austrian archduke's killing, but 'Murder' is a verb here and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate someone is a euphemism for killing them, so it serves as a verb synonym for murder.

clue.text: Avoid getting key cut

parts.note: the Escape key on a computer keyboard
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Steer clear of having a spare key made at the locksmith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key cut' looks like a locksmith's job, but the key is a keyboard key and 'cut' is a separate verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately abstain from or shun it, a formal synonym of avoid.

clue.text: Speaks about chateau's central supports

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the letter that follows

parts.note: to speak is to say

indicators.note: central refers to the exact middle, so only the middle letter of the building's name is used

parts.note: the fourth of the seven letters is the centre one

explanation.surface: Someone talks about the pillars holding up a French country house.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are props or bracing ropes that hold something up, such as a ship's mast, so they are supports.

clue.text: Mostly rustic housing before time of Galileo for instance

indicators.note: a house holds its contents within, so the shortened word surrounds the following letters
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for a country bumpkin is dropped

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated country person
archaic word meaning before
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something about country cottages built before the age of Galileo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time of Galileo' reads as a historical period, but 'time' is a lone abbreviation and Galileo is only an example for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo was condemned by the Inquisition for supporting heliocentrism, so he is a famous example of someone branded a heretic.

clue.text: More astute to frame old island philanderer

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so the first word surrounds what follows

parts.note: comparative of wise
standard abbreviation for old
the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A shrewder person sets out to stitch up a former islander who chases women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' suggests framing someone for a crime, but it simply means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: A philanderer is a man who has many casual affairs, which is exactly what a womaniser is.

clue.text: Information on fellow not specific

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a man's name, as crosswords often use for 'fellow'

explanation.surface: A vague report has been compiled about some man.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means applying to a whole class rather than to one particular thing, the opposite of specific.

clue.text: Stuff described by Ms West as ornamental knotted thread

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so the name encircles the word for stuff

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress
to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Mae West characterises some material as decorative knotted cord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Described' suggests speech, but here it means drawn around, as in describing a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is the craft of knotting cord or thread into decorative patterns, so it matches the definition directly.

clue.text: Swimmer from Germany finished with spirit reportedly

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
something finished is over

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for spirit is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the soul is a person's spirit

explanation.surface: A German swimmer finished the race in high spirits, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests an athlete, but it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dover sole is a flatfish from European waters, and in crosswords any fish can be called a swimmer.

clue.text: Woeful failure of musical to captivate audiences at the outset

indicators.note: to captivate is literally to hold captive, so the letters enclose another one
a failure is something that has fallen apart, so these letters break up and reform

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the outset is the very start, so only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A disastrous flop of a stage show that never won over its audiences from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a theatre review, but the musical itself is just letters to be rearranged with A.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamitous means disastrous or dreadful, so it is a synonym of woeful in the sense of deplorably bad.

clue.text: Minister to become widely discussed on X right away

indicators.note: away means removed, so the letter for right is taken out of the word

parts.note: a topic that trends on X (formerly Twitter) is widely talked about there
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A government minister is hoping to go viral on social media straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a politician, but 'Minister to' is a verb phrase meaning look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To minister to someone is to look after their needs, which is what it means to tend them.

clue.text: Letter from novelist about gripping opening of Germinal

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the novelist's name is read backwards
gripping means holding tight, so the turned name holds the single letter inside

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of Zola's novel's title

explanation.surface: A writer's letter discusses the gripping start of Zola's novel Germinal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, an example of a letter.

clue.text: Test Pearl devised for component of gunpowder

indicators.note: something devised is newly contrived, so the letters are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Pearl set an exam question about what goes into gunpowder.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the American spelling; British usage prefers saltpetre.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpeter, potassium nitrate, is the oxidising ingredient of black powder alongside charcoal and sulphur.

clue.text: Use of tax to protect oddly neglected deer

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it on all sides, so the tax word wraps around the kept letters

parts.note: excise is a duty on goods

indicators.note: if the odd positions are ignored, only the second and fourth letters of the animal survive

parts.note: the even letters of the word

explanation.surface: Tax money is spent on sheltering strangely abandoned deer.
explanation.walkthrough: Excise is a tax charged on goods such as alcohol and tobacco; the kept letters go after its first two.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or power is to put it to use, so the noun exercise can mean use.

clue.text: Utter devastation of aunt and niece

indicators.note: devastation is wreckage, so the following letters are smashed and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aunt and her niece are left in total ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning total, but it is the verb meaning say.
explanation.definitionFit: To enunciate is to pronounce or articulate words, so it is a verb synonym of utter.

clue.text: Ignorant of reason for O'Sullivan not playing around end of April

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the phrase's word goes round the single letter

parts.note: Ronnie O'Sullivan is a snooker champion, and he could not play without his cue

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is taken from the month

parts.note: last letter of the month

explanation.surface: Not knowing why the snooker star O'Sullivan withdrew from a tournament in late April.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie O'Sullivan is a famous English snooker player; a player lacking a cue would be cue-less, a word built for the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Clueless is informal for having no idea or knowledge about something, which is being ignorant.

clue.text: Items in diary showing guards absent at first

indicators.note: absent at first says the opening letter is missing, so the word loses its initial

parts.note: sentries are soldiers keeping guard

explanation.surface: A diary records that the guards were missing at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Entries are the individual records written into a diary, each one a separate item.

clue.text: Complete crackpot needing no introduction

indicators.note: an introduction is the first part, so needing none means the word's opening letter goes

parts.note: nutter is British slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A total eccentric so famous that nobody needs to introduce him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing no introduction' sounds like a compliment for a celebrity but means drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means absolute or total, as in 'utter nonsense', so it is an adjective synonym of complete.

clue.text: Labour right about trouble embracing alternative vote

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the outer letters surround the voting system
about can mean turned round, so the abbreviation for right is read backwards

parts.note: a common abbreviation for right
to ail is to trouble or afflict
AV is the abbreviation for the alternative vote electoral system

explanation.surface: The Labour Party's right wing is worried about a new voting system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party, given the talk of right and votes, but it is plain hard work. The alternative vote is a preferential voting system the UK rejected in 2011.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail means painful or laborious effort, so it is a noun synonym of labour.

clue.text: Notice some of stop signs facing the wrong way

indicators.note: facing the wrong way means pointing backwards, so the letters are read right to left
some of means only part of the following words, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: the last four letters of 'stop' with the first of 'signs'

explanation.surface: Pay attention to traffic signs that have been turned the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or catch sight of it, a verb synonym of notice.

clue.text: Delightful Democrat likely to attract votes in ballot

parts.note: standard abbreviation for Democrat

parts.words: likely to attract votes in ballot
parts.note: a candidate who could win an election

explanation.surface: A charming Democratic candidate who looks set to win an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable means delicious or very pleasing, so it is a synonym of delightful.

clue.text: The most worthless part remains

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the worst or least valuable portion
second meaning: the sediment left at the bottom of a cup or bottle

explanation.surface: The least valuable portion is what is left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one sentence with 'remains' as a verb, but 'remains' is a noun, the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the sediment left in a glass and, figuratively, the lowest or least valuable section of something.

clue.text: Take a brief look ignoring German weapon

parts.note: to glance is to look briefly
standard abbreviation for German

explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by a mounted knight, so it is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Hits Sainsbury's first with industrial action

parts.note: a strike is a withdrawal of labour

indicators.note: first means the opening position, so only the initial letter of the supermarket's name is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the supermarket chain's name

explanation.walkthrough: Sainsbury's is a major British supermarket chain. 'With' only joins, so the S goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike someone is to hit them, so the verb form strikes matches hits.

clue.text: South American girl crossing very open grassland

parts.note: standard abbreviation for south

indicators.note: crossing here means stretching across, so the outer letters span the one for very

parts.note: a girl's name
standard abbreviation for very
standard abbreviation for American

explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one description of the girl, but it is two abbreviations, S and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A savanna is a grassy plain with few trees, typical of tropical regions, so it is open grassland.

clue.text: Oppose Iceland stopping support

indicators.note: stopping can mean plugging a gap, so the country's code goes into the word for support

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a snooker cue or an arm
IS is the international code for Iceland

explanation.surface: Objecting to Iceland halting its backing for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to stand against it or fight it, a verb synonym of oppose.

clue.text: In all likelihood that's a boot

parts.note: as in 'it may well rain', meaning very probably
i.e. is short for id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Most probably that is some sort of footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: A wellie is a Wellington, a British rubber rain boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellie is a waterproof rubber boot reaching the knee, named after the Duke of Wellington, so it is a boot.
